clue.text: Insect found in place close to coast

parts.note: a locus is a place or position

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of coast

explanation.surface: A bug turns up somewhere near the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A locust is a large grasshopper that swarms and strips crops, so it is an example of an insect.

clue.text: Ball game in LA, trial reportedly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so go by how the word is spoken

parts.note: a cross to bear is a trial or burden

explanation.surface: A sports match is staged in Los Angeles, as a test run, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: LA looks like the city, but it is just two letters taken as they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with a small rubber ball carried in netted sticks.

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Something that used to be a seaplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying boat' reads as one aircraft term, but 'flying' is the signal and 'boat' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow vessel paddled through water, a type of small craft.

clue.text: Brief record of the suitable candidates

parts.note: brief means short
a list is a written record of items

explanation.surface: A concise note of which applicants are worth considering.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description, but the first two words build the answer and the rest defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the final selection of applicants judged good enough to be considered for a post.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bump or raised area on the body
second meaning: increasing in size, as a verb form

explanation.surface: A worrying growth on the body that keeps enlarging.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a puffed-up bump and the present participle of a verb meaning to expand.

indicators.note: one phrase sits on the outside of the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: to water down something is to moderate or dilute it
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A cinema review tempers its view of a dodgy smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrasal verb splits in two, with the joint sitting between its words.
explanation.definitionFit: Watership Down is the 1978 animated feature about rabbits, adapted from Richard Adams's novel.

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other, so it is placed second

parts.note: your lot is your fortune or fate
US stands for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A Yank chasing riches in exchange for a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus is a British sports car manufacturer, so a Lotus is a make of car.

clue.text: Run out in awfully big limo causes a jam

indicators.note: one piece goes in, inside the other
done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these two words
ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A stretch limousine running out of control gridlocks the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter dismissed run out is recorded as 'ro'.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, complicated situation, and a jam in the sense of a tight spot or mess.

clue.text: Voracious animal up in heart of Argyll

indicators.note: one piece goes in, placed inside the other
the heart of a word is its middle, so only its central letters are wanted

parts.note: the two central letters of Argyll

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: A hungry beast heading north into the Scottish highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Argyll is a region of western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy means having an excessive appetite, which is what voracious describes.

clue.text: A short time after state capital makes pact

indicators.note: one piece follows the other, so it is placed second

parts.note: Concord is the capital of New Hampshire
taken as written
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Not long after reaching the capital, a treaty is signed.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially between the Vatican and a state, so a pact.

indicators.note: something lunatic is crazy and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A detested, rebellious madman at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolshy is British slang for uncooperative or bolshevik-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotheboys Hall is the brutal Yorkshire boarding school run by Wackford Squeers in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby.

indicators.note: one word goes round about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a tale is a lie, as in telling tales
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Someone fibbing about a UK graph.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is an arrangement of data in rows and columns, a kind of chart.

parts.note: over means finished, at an end

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter, which is the one kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Turnberry

explanation.surface: A golfer's tournament ended, with someone coming top at the Turnberry Open.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnberry is a Scottish links course that has hosted golf's Open Championship, so 'open' looks like the tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and not concealed, so it is a synonym of the adjective open.

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A burglar was briefly detained, busted at the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the strip of floor at the bottom of a door, so it stands for the entrance or doorway.

clue.text: Lies in patches around part of the Vatican

indicators.note: letters strewn around are scattered and land in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Untruths scattered here and there throughout the papal city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In patches' sounds like the scattering signal, but those words are letters to be rearranged; 'around' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sistine Chapel, with Michelangelo's ceiling, is a chapel within the Vatican's Apostolic Palace.

clue.text: Rash yet fasten a protective device

indicators.note: acting rashly means acting wildly, so the letters are put into a reckless new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Reckless, yet secure a guard against falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety net is a mesh hung below acrobats to catch a fall, so it is a device for protection.

clue.text: Father, in capital, wants us raised together

indicators.note: one word goes in, inside the other

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad, living in the city, would like the family brought up there too.
explanation.definitionFit: Pari passu is Latin for 'with equal step', meaning side by side or simultaneously.

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym lessons

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A drama staged in a sports hall featuring the upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer Gynt is Ibsen's verse drama, so it is the name of a stage play.

indicators.note: letters sent abroad wander widely and return in a different order

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An apt proposal that I back overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit for purpose describes something good enough to do the job intended, which is what suitable means.

clue.text: Criticise American standing on a hat

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece standing on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
Am is the abbreviation for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: Knocking a US citizen who is standing on a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight straw hat with a brim, originally woven in Ecuador.

clue.text: A new piece of advice about hors d'oeuvre

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a tip is a helpful hint
as to means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A fresh hint on what to serve before the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it signals letters going round something, but it simply gives the two-word phrase as to.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables, an appetiser served before the meal.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who strikes poses for a photographer

explanation.surface: A tricky interview question put to a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tough puzzle and a person who poses, such as an artist's sitter.

indicators.note: one piece goes in, placed inside the other

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of played

explanation.surface: A performer who played first as backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays the bagpipes or pipe, which makes him or her a musician.

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their usual order

parts.note: the letters of this word
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Liveliness combined with remarkable drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a throb of life or a vital rhythm, so it stands for liveliness and energy.

clue.text: Miss Grey, from the north, kept in a long time

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: ages means a long time
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A grey-haired spinster from up north, detained for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Agnes Grey is the title heroine of Anne Brontë's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Anne Brontë's novel is the unmarried governess Agnes Grey, so she is that Miss Grey.

parts.note: an aunt is a relative, plus the possessive s
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A family member's teammate in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a traditional English pub and fairground game of throwing sticks at a dummy's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunt Sally names the British throwing pastime and also a target of easy criticism; here it is the pastime.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coming behind every other one
second meaning: nevertheless, despite what has happened

explanation.surface: Finishing bottom, despite all efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means following every other, i.e. final; as an idiom it means nevertheless.

parts.note: RU is rugby union
pert means lively and jaunty

explanation.surface: A plucky, cheerful fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like an adjective for brave, matching the surface, but it is the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert is a man's first name, and in crosswords any male name can be clued as a chap.
